questions.question: Who among the following is a famous performer of the Kathakali classical dance?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is a famous performer of the Kathakali classical dance?

The correct answer is Gopinath.

Key Points

  • Guru Gopinath broadened the boundaries of tradition while maintaining the traditional discipline that kept him in check.
  • He played a significant role in bringing Kerala's renowned dance theatre, Kathakali, out of obscurity and into the public eye.
  • Like Uday Shankar, he is regarded as one of the legendary figures of Indian dance in the 20th century.
  • He developed a modern dance form that was classical in form but had a broad appeal, by which Kathakali's renown quickly expanded throughout the world from the start of the 1930s.

Additional Information

    • The entire male troop performs in kathakali.
    • Keralan temple dancing is known as Kathakali.

questions.question: Who was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022?
questions.questionHtml: Who was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vinai Kumar Saxena.

Key Points

  • The Delhi National Capital Territory's constitutional governor is the lieutenant governor.
  • On May 26, 2022, Shri Vinai Kumar Saxena became the 22nd Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
  • Shri Saxena, 63, is the first corporate man to be chosen for such a gubernatorial position.
  • He has more than three decades of extensive expertise in the corporate and social sectors.

Additional Information

  •  Lieutenant Governor
    • ​In the Republic of India, a lieutenant governor is the constitutional head of five out of the eight union territories.
    • The lieutenant governor is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years and holds office at the President's pleasure.
    • Since the union territories of Delhi, Jammu, and Kashmir, and Puducherry have a measure of self-government with an elected legislature and council of ministers, the role of the lieutenant governor there is mostly a ceremonial one, akin to that of a state's governor.
    • In Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Ladakh however, the lieutenant governor holds more power, being both the head of state and head of government.

questions.question: Which of the following has unit m/s 2 ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following has unit m/s<sup>2</sup>?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Acceleration.

Key Points

  • Acceleration
    • The rate at which an object's velocity with respect to time changes is referred to as acceleration.
    • A vector quantity is an acceleration (has magnitude and direction both).
    • LT-2 or meter per second square(m/s2) is the unit of acceleration.

Additional Information

  • Speed 
    • A scalar quantity, speed is defined as the magnitude of the rate at which an object's position changes over time.
    • The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of speed.
  • Velocity
    • The pace at which an object's position changes in relation to a frame of reference is known as its velocity, which is a time-dependent quantity.
    • A description of an object's speed and direction of motion is what is meant by its velocity.
    • The quantity is a vector.
    • The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of velocity.
  • Distance
    • The International System of Units defines a meter as the distance unit. It's interesting to note that many other derived units or quantities, such as volume, area, acceleration, and speed, may be constructed using this as the basic unit and a few formulae.
    • The meter(m) is the SI unit of length.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unit of distance?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a unit of distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Light year.

Key Points:

  • The unit of length used to express astronomical distances is the light year, which is roughly comparable to 5.88 trillion miles or 9.46 trillion kilometres.
  • According to the International Astronomical Union (IAU), a light-year is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in one Julian year (365.25 days).
  • Since "light-year" incorporates the term "year," which designates a unit of measurement for time, it is occasionally misinterpreted as a unit of time.
  • The light-year is most typically used to depict distances to stars and other distances on a galactic scale, especially in non-specialist contexts and popular science publications.
  • The measuring unit most frequently used in professional astronomy is the parsec, which is derived from astrometry and equals 3.26 light-years. 

Additional Information:

  • Newton: 
    • A newton is a unit of force in the International System of Units (symbol: N).
    • 1 kgm/s2 is the force that accelerates a mass of one kilogramme by one metre per second square.
    • It is named after Isaac Newton.
  • Watt:
    • ​The electrical power determined in Watts is the equivalent of one ampere under one volt of pressure.
  • Joule:
    • ​The work performed by a force of one newton acting through one metre is equivalent to one joule, a unit of work or energy in the International System of Units (SI).

questions.question: What is the LCM of (8x 3 + 80x 2 + 200x) and (4x 4 + 16x 3 - 20x 2 )?

questions.solution:
If we factorise (8x3 + 80x2 + 200x) and (4x4 + 16x3 - 20x2) we get,

8x3 + 80x2 + 200x ⇒ 8x(x2 + 10x + 25) ⇒ 8x(x2 + 5x + 5x + 25) ⇒ 8x(x + 5)(x + 5)

Again, 4x4 + 16x3 - 20x2 ⇒ 4x2 (x2 + 4x - 5) ⇒ 4x2 (x2 - x + 5x - 5) ⇒ 4x2 (x - 1)(x+ 5)

Now, LCM of the two polynomials is 8x2(x + 5)2(x - 1)

(25M + 45W) × 15 = (15M + 60W) × 20

Time = Total work / Efficiency = 3300 / 550 = 6 days

questions.question: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
questions.questionHtml: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
questions.solution:
Vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, and P wins the race by 8 sec, which means P travels 1500 m and Q travels 1300 m

Speed of P = \(\frac{1500}{t}\) and speed of Q = \(\frac{1300}{t+8}\)   [Let the time taken by P is t]

Now, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, race is draw, which means P travels 1500 m and Q travels 1100 m

\(\frac{1500}{\frac{1500}{t}}=\frac{1100}{\frac{1300}{t+8}}\) ⇒  \(t=\frac{11(t+8)}{13}\) ⇒ 2t = 88 ⇒ t = 44 sec
